page: Microsoft Azure HB368rs_v5 is a high-performance computing instance built on dedicated x86_64 Intel processors and the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The virtual machine provides 368 dedicated vCPUs paired with 448.0 GB of system memory, resulting in an allocation of 1.22 GB of RAM per vCPU. It features RDMA networking capability to support tightly coupled multi-node computational clusters, alongside support for Premium Storage tiers.

Storage infrastructure on the instance includes 15,874 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD capacity. It does not bundle discrete GPU hardware. The combination of massive local NVMe disk volume and dedicated processor cores enables fast disk scratch operations and reduces data transfer bottlenecks during intensive localized data staging.

Because memory is allocated at a lean 1.22 GB per core, the architecture emphasizes raw computational parallelization over memory-heavy caching. This makes the server cost-efficient for parallel tasks that scale horizontally across compute cores. Target workloads include MPI-based scientific simulations, computational fluid dynamics, finite element analysis, weather forecasting models, and large-scale parallel processing jobs.
